1 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE NARENDRA SINGH DHADDHA Judgment DATE OF JUDGMENT 15/02/2024

The present appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the claimants-appellants (for short 'the claimants') dissatisfied with the judgment and award dated 14.03.2023 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ajmer (for short 'the Tribunal') in MAC No.563/2015, whereby the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.5,30,600/- along with interest @ 9% per annum from the date of filing the claim petition as compensation in favour of the claimants.
The Tribunal on the basis of the pleading of the parties, framed the issues and evaluated the evidence on record.
After hearing counsel for the parties, decided the claim petition of the claimant and awarded the amount as indicated above.
Learned counsel for the claimants submits that the Tribunal has wrongly considered the income of the deceased as Rs. 3,000/- per month.

Learned counsel for the claimants submits that claimants had submitted the cogent evidence that deceased was earning Rs. 10,000/- per month, so, income of the deceased be calculated as Rs. 10,000/- per month.

Learned counsel for the claimants also submits that the Tribunal has wrongly awarded a lumpsum amount of Rs. 44,000/- to the claimant Nos. 1 and 2 towards filial consortium whereas it should be Rs. 40,000/- to each claimant towards filial consortium and loss of love and affection.
So, the judgment and award of the Tribunal be modified accordingly.

Learned counsel for the insurance company has opposed the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the claimants and submits that the claimants had not adduced any cogent evidence regarding income of the deceased as Rs. 10,000/- per month.
[CMA-1493/2023] the Tribunal had rightly assessed the income of the deceased as Rs. 3,000/- per month.
Learned counsel for the insurance company also submits that the Tribunal has rightly awarded Rs. 44,000/- towards filial consortium.
So, the appeal filed by the claimants be dismissed.
I have considered the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the claimants as well as the insurance company.
It is an admitted position that claimants had not adduced any cogent evidence regarding income of the deceased as Rs. 10,000/- per month.
So, in my considered opinion the Tribunal has rightly assessed the income of the deceased as Rs. 3,000/- per month.

The Tribunal has awarded Rs.
44,000/- towards filial consortium to claimant Nos. 1 and 2, whereas it should be Rs. 40,000/- to each claimant.
So, claimants are entitled to get Rs. 40,000/- per person towards filial consortium and loss of love and affection instead of Rs. 44,000/- lump sum.
So, the judgment of the Tribunal is modified to the extent as under:-

Monthly income Rs.3,000/-
 Annual Income 3,000 X12= Rs.36,000/-
 1/2 is to be deducted for 36,000 - 18,000=18,000/-
 personal expenses of the  deceased

According to the age of the 18,000X18= Rs.3,24,000/-

Enhanced Amount of  compensation   
In view of the above, the claimants are entitled to get a further sum of Rs. 1,56,000/- as compensation.

The insurance company is directed to deposit enhanced amount of Rs. 1,56,000/-
(6,86,600 - 5,30,600= Rs.1,56,000/-) with the Tribunal within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this order.
On deposition of the said amount, the claimants shall be entitled to withdraw the same.
The enhanced amount shall carry @ 9% interest per annum.
Rest part of the impugned judgment shall remain unchanged.
Impugned judgment and award is modified accordingly.
Consequently, the appeal is partly allowed.
Pending application(s), if any, also stand(s) disposed of.
